top.title: AI boom threatens circuit board crunch to rival pandemic-era chip shortage
top.description: The electronics industry faces a printed circuit board (PCB) shortage that could rival the pandemic-era chip crunch – with AI once again accused of hogging supplies. The Global Electronics Association says demand is arriving "at a scale the supply chain was not built for," straining everything from glass fabric and resin to finished boards. Its report, " The PCB Squeeze: A Wake-Up Call for Global Electronics ," says AI servers need increasingly complex boards. While a typical PC board has about 12 layers of tracks, AI server boards can have 40 to 60 layers or more, and each additional layer requires more resin, copper foil, and laminate. The supply of materials is set to be constrained through at least the first half of 2027, the report says, with meaningful relief unlikely before mid-2028. Programs to deliver PCBs for automotive, industrial, medical and even the defense industries are being crowded out as AI soaks up scarce capacity, it claims. The association's North American figures show orders growing much faster than deliveries. PCB bookings rose 56.1 percent in the first nine months of 2026 compared with the same period last year, while PCB shipments increased 13.3 percent. Fabrication capacity is expanding, aimed at meeting the increased demand from the AI infrastructure sector, especially in Asia, where more than 90 percent of the world's boards are made. The report says that $10 billion has gone toward new PCB plants in Southeast Asia, and at least as much has been invested in China over the past three years, but the raw materials are themselves constrained. It warns of lengthening lead times for those raw materials. Standard FR-4 laminate now takes six to eight weeks to ship, up from two to three weeks a year ago, while advanced low-loss laminates now take 14 to 18 weeks for delivery, for example. Tightening supplies usually lead to price increases, and the report says that suppliers raised laminate costs by 30 percent in September, and that the price tag of some types of E-glass cloth for circuit boards has risen by 300 percent. The report also puts copper prices up 37 percent over the past year. Concerns have been raised about copper supplies before, as The Register has reported multiple times. The association compares the risk with the 2021 chip shortage , when disrupted supplies left manufacturers unable to secure even relatively mundane components. New capacity is coming, but it is late and comes in dribs and drabs, according to the report, while AI demand just keeps on absorbing it as soon as it arrives. The association's advice is for buyers to plan early, and to share realistic forecasts with suppliers rather than double-booking. Board makers should qualify alternative suppliers of materials such as laminate and copper foil before shortages bite, but it warns against stockpiling beyond real need, which adds to forward-buying pressure. But it would like governments to step in, of course, by tracking board and material lead times

top.title: Bitcoin Price Crashes to $59,000 as Market Selloff Deepens
top.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Crashes to $59,000 as Market Selloff Deepens The bitcoin price crashed below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since early July, falling about $1,800 in roughly an hour as a deepening U.S. tech stock selloff dragged risk assets lower. Bitcoin traded near $61,400 at 9:40 a.m. ET and slid to about $59,600 by 10:45 a.m., a drop of nearly 3%, according to Look Into Bitcoin data . The bitcoin price is down about $3,400, or more than 5%, from the same time Thursday, when it traded near $63,000. The break of $60,000 is a key psychological level, and it came with little warning. Bitcoin price had held above $61,000 for most of the morning, even after a third straight daily loss. Stocks and rate hike bets drive the selloff Wall Street opened sharply lower. The Nasdaq Composite fell more than 2% in morning trading as shares of Anthropic extended losses in its second day since a record Nasdaq debut. Nvidia and AMD also traded lower. Bitcoin has been moving with tech stocks. The market has questioned whether heavy spending on artificial intelligence will pay off, and Friday’s open did nothing to ease that worry. Rate expectations are adding pressure. Traders see a roughly 94% chance the Federal Reserve raises rates in December, CME Group’s FedWatch tool showed . Higher rates tend to hurt bitcoin and other assets that pay no yield. Earlier Friday, South Korea’s Kospi index fell more than 5% and chipmakers sank across Asia. That selling carried into U.S. trading and then into bitcoin. Some analysts had flagged $60,000 as a floor. Katie Stockton of Fairlead Strategies told CNBC the bottom of bitcoin’s trading range sits “just below 60,000,” and that it “appears to be trying to find a footing.” Friday’s drop tests that view. CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said this week the drop is a “continuation of the existing bear market.” His base case is range trading around $60,000 to $90,000 through much of 2027. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) lost $541.1 million on Thursday, its biggest one-day outflow on record. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $582 million in total, extending a streak of heavy withdrawals this week. Leveraged traders were hit as well. Alberts, who is leaving Texas A&M to become Michigan’s next athletic director, is expected to begin his new role on Dec. 1. top.title: Filming training by drones should be illegal - Iraola
top.description: Andoni Iraola's Liverpool take on Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United on Sunday [Getty Images] Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola says filming with drones around training grounds should be illegal after Mauricio Pochettino's first session as Manchester United boss was captured and uploaded online. Pochettino and his players were clearly visible in the footage, which was shot above United's Carrington training base from a variety of angles and distances. The drone operater apologised and later took down the footage, with sources telling BBC Sport they are adamant there was no security breach and that they do not intend to take legal action. Iraola said he was sent the 12 minutes of footage on Thursday - three days before United travel to Anfield for a Premier League match. "The important part of this is that it shouldn't be legal," he said on Friday. "It happened to United but it could happen to me. "Yesterday, when Sky Sports had access to our training and the cameras recorded 15-20 minutes, you know who trained and who didn't. "It's not the matter of the advantage. It's the fact that someone can do this. There's a reason we train behind closed doors because there are some things that you have to respect. I don't think it's nice for any club." Ten outfield players were seen working directly with former United States boss Pochettino in the footage, though it seems unlikely they will all start Sunday's match. "We've faced each other and obviously he [Pochettino] has a lot of Premier League games behind him that we can look at," said Iraola. "We can look at games from the US but it's true that they have this small advantage that we don't have references to prepare, because they can go different ways that we honestly don't know right now." Iraola said he expected United to be "well prepared" as Pochettino's assistants travelled to England to work with the players before the Argentine arrived on Wednesday. "They have this advantage that we don't exactly know - or at least we don't have the references like we do against other opposition," he said. "Especially the beginning of the game will be important. We have to adapt to certain things. But we know the players very well." Liverpool are fourth in the table - 14 places ahead of United. But they have failed to beat the Red Devils at Anfield in each of the past three seasons, and have lost to Arsenal and Manchester City at home already in this campaign. "You don't find bigger games than this," said Iraola. "I feel lucky to be here and privileged to be a part of these games. "We have to acknowledge the importance of the game. There are a lot of ingredients. They have a new manager, new challenges for us. This is important for us in a lot of different ways. "We want to improve our form at home. We have been very good away but not good at home and the first chance we have is United on Sunday." Pochettino training session filmed by drone - what did we learn? top.description: RB Leipzig v Manchester City - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 - Getty Images Sport Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has called for a sense of perspective as his side prepares to return to Premier League action against Fulham. Following a dip in results before the international break, the Italian tactician is determined to shield his high-profile stars from mounting external pressure. Finding stability amid the noise Reflecting on the recent run of results, Maresca emphasised the need for a measured approach, particularly after a spectacular start to his first Premier League season in charge of City, which saw him guide the team to a record seven consecutive wins - the best start to a managerial reign in the competition's history. However, City suffered three defeats in their following matches before the international break , which ends with Saturday's home clash against Fulham. 'I think there is always a reason why you win a game or you lose a game, no doubt. But it is a matter of balance,' Maresca explained. 'We were not perfect at the beginning when we were winning games and we've not been so bad when we lost the last three games. So that's why it is a matter of finding the right balance between the two things. And again, with the new players, a new manager, it is part of the process.' Maresca is well aware that even the most successful seasons are rarely without obstacles. He reminded supporters that adversity is a natural ingredient in the hunt for silverware. 'In all of the season when you achieve something important, you also go through difficult moments. I was here in the Treble season and we had some bad moments. It is normal and it is part of the season to drop some points, even more when you start something new like in our case with a new manager, new players and everything has changed.' Standing by Donnarumma Individual scrutiny has intensified during the break, particularly regarding Gianluigi Donnarumma. The Italian goalkeeper endured a challenging period with the national team in the UEFA Nations League, notably committing a high-profile error that allowed France to take the lead in Italy's 3-1 victory, before conceding four goals against Belgium. He has also made several costly mistakes for Manchester City during the 2026-27 season, including an error against Aston Villa that allowed Nicolas Jackson to score, leaving his near post exposed against RB Leipzig as Ridle Baku found the net from a tight angle, and facing criticism for his performance in City's 4-2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League. Maresca offered a full defence of his number one , acknowledging the errors while pointing to his shot-stopping qualities. 'He has been good,' Maresca said of Donnarumma. top.title: Maresca says struggling Man City not distracted by 'noise' around club
top.description: Enzo Maresca's Manchester City have lost their past three Premier League matches (Darren Staples) Enzo Maresca insists his Manchester City players are not distracted by the "noise" around the club's financial-rules case as he seeks to end their losing run. City flew out of the blocks in the Premier League this season, winning their first seven games, but three straight defeats have left them six points behind leaders Arsenal. The 10-time English champions are still waiting to discover the extent of their punishment after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules. The club have repeatedly denied wrongdoing and have appealed against the verdict. But Maresca said he did not believe the case was weighing on the minds of his third-placed team ahead of their match against Fulham at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday. "I don't think the players are thinking too much about that," he said, "If we want to relate the noise with the defeats, Villa away, I think we had so many chances... Brighton here, the keeper was the man of the match. "The Forest one (a 3-1 defeat), where Erling (Haaland) had the chance to (make it) 2-2. I don't think the players are focused on the noise." Maresca admitted his side needed to improve but said not everything was perfect even when they were winning. "Overall, we control the game almost every time," said the Italian. "There are moments when we don't control the game and it is a moment when we need to understand the reason why and to do better." The former Chelsea boss, who replaced Pep Guardiola in the close-season, pointed out that he had not been at City for long, stressing his focus is on the long term. "Probably you forget a little bit about the time we spent together," he said. "It is not a big time that we are together. That is why I can see that what we are working on every day is there. "This is a good thing, it is a nice feeling. Also, the work we are doing is helping the players to be better players and to be a better team. For me, it is just the beginning of something long." City can take heart from their eye-catching 20-game winning run against Fulham in all competitions. "I didn't know that it's 20 games, hopefully 21," said Maresca. top.title: The tale of the Wolves fans who did not return from a world cup to be shown
top.description: The documentary follows the adventures of a group of Wolves fans who went to the Mexico World Cup in 1986 and never came back to the UK [Gary Allen] A screening of a documentary about a group of Wolves fans who went to the 1986 World Cup in Mexico and did not return to the Black Country will take place at the club. The group decided not to return to their Stourbridge and Lye homes after attending the global football spectacular, embarking on new lives in the US instead. Gary Allen, who settled in Atlanta and who pitched the documentary, said "Wolves called us and said 'would you like to do the first screening in the UK at the Molineux? And of course all being Wolves fans we said 'we'd love to'." Lost Down Mexico Way will be shown at Molineux on Friday evening, just one part of reunion gatherings this week. The stars of the documentary are referred to by their nicknames. As well as Allen, known as Adder, it features Rabbithead (Garry Hardwicke), Batesy (Stuart Bates), Arnie (David Arnold) and Texas Steve (Steve Dawson). After the World Cup and a brief jaunt to Belize, the gang flew to Dallas, Texas. Gary Allen, known as Adder, said "before you know it, there's 40 years gone" [Gary Allen] The group had lived in the Black Country all their lives before flying 5,000 miles to experience the 1986 tournament. Allen, who retired from running his own company last year, has previously said the "opportunity was the biggest thing for us", as he talked about the US. "I think back in 86... the job situation wasn't the best back then. "I'd just lost my job, [Margaret] Thatcher was in power, a few of the lads were just doing painting and whatever. "We'd all saved a bit of money and the idea was to go out there and do a few weeks and just travel. We just played it by ear really." Allen added once "we got there and enjoyed it, it just went from there and we all stayed and then more and more came over". "And before you know it, there's 40 years gone," he said. "So it was just a chance we took back in the day and luckily it's panned out well for us." Of those attending, a coach from Stourbridge was leaving on Friday afternoon "and about four or five carloads". "So we've got 80 [in] total that Wolves have given us tickets for, so it should be a good reunion," Allen added. Allen said he was looking forward to having a "good chat, good reminisce". "As you get older you can't do it. "So this is a one-off and it'll be the last time I see a lot of people, but it's gonna be great and we'll certainly make the most of it." top.title: Report Milan ready to sell Estupinan and Loftus-Cheek, loan young talent out
top.description: Report Milan ready to sell Estupinan and Loftus-Cheek, loan young talent out Milan are expected to sell Pervis Estupinan and Ruben Loftus-Cheek in the January transfer window, with Turkish and English clubs interested, while Francesco Camarda and Christian Comotto are heading on loan. The Rossoneri have stuttered so far this season and found significant differences between the first choice team’s performance and those who come in during squad rotation. This has prompted three defeats out of four Europa League games so far, and coach Ruben Amorim is reportedly ready to cut some players loose. Milan clear out dead wood JAKARTA, INDONESIA – AUGUST 08: Pervis Estupinan of AC Milan controls the ball against Pedro Neto of Chelsea FC during the pre-season friendly between Chelsea FC and AC Milan at Gelora Bung Karno Stadium on August 08, 2026 in Jakarta, Indonesia. (Photo by Peksi Cahyo/Getty Images) Amorim had declared at the start of the season that he convinced Milan to keep hold of Estupinan when a move to Aston Villa had been practically agreed. Now several months on, he seemingly regrets that decision and has given the all-clear for an exit, but the Premier League side is no longer interested. A loan move to Fiorentina could be on the cards , although they hope to find a more permanent solution to make back some of that investment. ITALY – SEPTEMBER 14: Ruben Loftus-Cheek of AC Milan in action during the Serie A match between AC Milan and Bologna FC 1909 at Giuseppe Meazza Stadium on September 14, 2025 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Loftus-Cheek is only under contract with the Rossoneri until the end of this season, but persistent injuries and poor performances should see him sold in January. Coventry City had made an approach in the summer, and could well try again, but Besiktas and other Turkish teams are also options. Francesco Camarda scores from the penalty spot during a pre-season friendly between Celtic and Milan at Celtic Park (via www.acmilan.com) Meanwhile, young players Camarda and Comotto are clearly not going to get a chance to deliver, so will be sent out on loan in January to gain valuable experience. Genoa are the most advanced in talks for midfielder Comotto, while Camarda has numerous proposals from Serie A, B, and even abroad.

top.description: FILE PHOTO - USA manager and new Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino during press conference at the Arthur M. Blank National Training Centre. Pochettino has been appointed as Manchester United head coach from November 18, the club have announced. Pochettino addressed the media for the first time as United boss on Friday, two days before the trip to face old rivals Liverpool – a match United will start inside the relegation zone. United’s recent recruitment has come in for heavy criticism with a feeling that Pochettino’s predecessor Michael Carrick was left short-handed by the club’s summer business, overseen by director of football Jason Wilcox. While he has accepted the title of head coach, former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino made clear he wants to have a big say behind the scenes. “Since I started at Espanyol, head coach, coach, manager…in the end it’s not changing too much, because I think the way that we work is indifferent to the title description,” Pochettino said. “Sometimes I worked much better when I was head coach or when I was coach than manager, and it’s not necessarily that if you are manager you have all the decisions. Maybe you are a coach and have more power in the decision. “It depends on the structure, depends on the communication, depends on the relationship with all the areas. I know that being a head coach I am the guy that is going to decide the squad for Sunday, I’m going to pick the starting 11 and make the changes. “Of course in the future I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that will happen on the squad. In the end Manchester United is a football club.” One decision Pochettino has already made is that Bruno Fernandes will remain as club captain. top.title: Alcaraz concerned over fitness despite win over Cobolli at ATP Finals
top.description: FILE PHOTO - Team Europe's Carlos Alcaraz in action against Team World's Taylor Fritz during the men's singles group stage match on day two of the Laver Cup tennis tournament at The O2. (is associated with: «Alcaraz concerned over fitness despite win over Cobolli at ATP Finals») Adam Davy/PA Wire/dpa Carlos Alcaraz remains concerned about his fitness despite a straightforward victory over Flavio Cobolli at the ATP Finals. The Spaniard extended his winning run to 12 matches with his third straight-sets win in Turin, seeing off Italian Cobolli 6-4, 6-1. Alcaraz, who had already booked his spot in the last four, arrived in Italy with concerns over a right knee niggle and took a medical timeout to have his left hamstring strapped during a victory over Daniil Medvedev on Wednesday. There had been speculation he might pull out and, although he appears in great form, Alcaraz admitted his physical struggles are a worry. He said on atptour.com: “The challenge is no longer on the court, it is off the court, to do whatever it takes to be physically ready for the match tomorrow. It is going to be a really important next day.” Alcaraz is scheduled to take on Ben Shelton in the last four on Saturday. Britain’s Neal Skupski and his American partner Christian Harrison booked their spot in the doubles semi-finals with a 7-6 (7-5), 6-4 victory over third seeds Marcel Granollers and Horacio Zeballos. Meanwhile, ATP Tour chair Andrea Gaudenzi defended his absence from the ceremony earlier this week honouring world number one doubles pair Henry Patten and Harri Heliovaara. Gaudenzi was present during a similar ceremony for singles number one Alexander Zverev and Patten publicly criticized his decision not to attend. The row comes against the backdrop of controversial plans to reduce prize money and opportunity for doubles players on the men’s tour, of which Patten has been a leading critic. Gaudenzi told a press conference that the ceremony had clashed with an important meeting, saying: “I can guarantee it was not done intentionally to deliver a message. Not at all. We wouldn’t be that silly, because we know that the situation is tense now. “I have had a meeting with Harri and the working group of doubles in Paris for hours until 8pm. I understand it’s emotional for them. I feel the pain for them.” Gaudenzi added that there is not yet consensus on the proposals, with further discussions planned for next month.

top.title: Manchester United travel to Anfield with 'advantage' claims Andoni Iraola despite drone footage
top.description: Andoni Iraola's Liverpool will host Manchester United on Sunday -Credit:Gaspafotos/MB Media, Getty Images Andoni Iraola has argued that it is Liverpool who will be at a disadvantage when they face Manchester United at Anfield on Sunday. United head into the weekend sitting 18th in the Premier League table with just one win from their opening 10 matches. The fixture will mark Mauricio Pochettino's first game at the helm since arriving from his previous role in the United States on Wednesday. Pochettino faces an enormous challenge in turning around his underperforming squad, and his preparations were further complicated when a rogue drone operator filmed his first training session on Thursday and posted the footage to YouTube. The 12-minute clip has since been removed , but appeared to expose details of Pochettino's tactical preparations on the training ground. Mauricio Pochettino took charge of his first training session with Manchester United on Thursday -Credit:Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images Iraola acknowledged that he had been sent the video and, while expressing sympathy for Pochettino, dismissed the notion that United had been placed at a disadvantage by the drone incident. "They sent me yesterday the footage," Iraola said in his pre-match press conference via The Mirror . "But I think the important part is that it shouldn't be legal. It happened to United but it could happen today to me in training you know. "Yesterday you had access to our training, the cameras in the corridors for 15 or 20 minutes, I don't know how much. You know who's training with us, who didn't train. We know the same (with United). "But it's not [about] the matter of the advantage, it's about the fact that someone can do this... I think there's a reason we train behind closed doors because there are some things that you have to respect and I don't think it's nice for any club, honestly." nigeria.title: Viral Video: Military uniforms found with bandits not from us – DHQ
nigeria.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Defence headquarters has denied supplying military camouflage uniforms allegedly found in the possession of suspected bandits in a viral social media video, insisting that the clothing did not originate from the Nigerian military. Read Also: The footage, circulating widely online, showed large quantities of woodland and desert camouflage uniforms spread on the ground, Several others were packed in sacks and allegedly held by suspected bandits. Reacting to the video, the Director of Defence Media Operations, Maj. Gen. Michael Onoja ruled out the possibility that the uniforms were supplied by the military. “That is not possible,” he said, when asked whether the clothing originated from the Nigerian military. Onoja also dismissed suggestions that the uniforms might have been stolen from military supply vehicles attacked by bandits, saying no such incident had been reported. “No such report has been made. It is not from the Nigerian military,” he added. The video reportedly showed two different camouflage patterns, identified as woodland and desert designs, raising renewed concerns over the circulation of military clothing among criminal groups and unauthorised persons. The development comes amid longstanding concerns about criminals, impersonating security personnel to perpetrate attacks, kidnappings and other crimes. In February 2024, the Federal Government reiterated restrictions on the unauthorised use of military camouflage by civilians, warning against the misuse of security uniforms and equipment by criminal elements Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle had stated that the restrictions were necessary to enable security agencies to distinguish legitimate personnel from impostors. He noted that criminals had exploited military and other security agencies’ uniforms to deceive members of the public and facilitate criminal activities. The government’s position was aimed at curbing impersonation, preventing the misuse of military uniforms and strengthening security operations across the country. nigeria.title: Boat capsizes with 300 passengers in Bayelsa
nigeria.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa A tragedy struck the riverine enclave of Southern Ijaw Local Government Area on Friday, as a cargo boat conveying over 300 passengers capsized, leaving many feared dead. The ill-fated vessel was reportedly en route to Ukubie community from Anyama Ijaw, when the incident occurred at 12 noon. According to preliminary reports, the boat, which was heavily overloaded with passengers traveling for a burial ceremony, went down in the waterways between Oweikorogha and Angiama communities. Eyewitness accounts indicate that the tragedy might have been averted. It was learned that some passengers had suggested the boat stop at Oweikorogha to decongest the vessel, but the advice was allegedly ignored. The boat reportedly capsized shortly after departing the community. While the actual casualty figure remains unconfirmed, fears are mounting that the death toll could be substantial given the number of persons on board. Mr. Ipigansi Igoniba, Chairman of the State Maritime Workers Union, confirmed the incident to our correspondent but stated that information regarding the disaster was still hazy. “I cannot give the casualty figure right now. We have sent our members to the scene of the accident and search and rescue efforts for the missing persons are ongoing,” Igoniba said. Rescue operations are currently underway, though independent confirmation of the number of survivors or fatalities is yet to be established. The incident has cast a pall of mourning over the community, highlighting once again the dangers of overcrowding and unsafe travel on the state’s waterways. nigeria.description: MultiChoice Nigeria has introduced restructured DStv and GOtv subscription packages, with entry-level options starting at ₦6,000, following customer feedback on affordability and content preferences. The company’s Chief Executive Officer, Kemi Omotosho, disclosed this during an interview on the Global Business Report on ARISE News on Friday, saying the new packages were designed to simplify subscription choices and provide customers with access to entertainment, sports and other content. She said the company had listened to its subscribers and adjusted its offerings to better address their needs. “We recognised that our customers are dear to us, so we listened to our customers, we simplified our offerings,” she said. Under the new arrangement, DStv subscribers can choose from four packages: Starter, Select, Sports and Premium, while GOtv offers Easy, Starter, Select and Sports. Omotosho said the Starter package, which costs ₦6,000, provides access to more than 90 channels, including Africa Magic Plus, the Premier League Match of the Week, selected UEFA Champions League matches and La Liga coverage. She also explained that the Sports package had been redesigned from the former Compact offering to provide broader access to major sporting competitions. According to her, the package includes all Premier League and Champions League matches, as well as UFC and WWE content, alongside channels available on the Starter and Select packages. Clarifying the subscription rates, Omotosho said the Sports package costs ₦21,000 for new subscribers, while the ₦19,000 rate applies only to existing Compact subscribers migrating to the new package. “When you move into the new pack, it’s ₦21,000 on the Sports pack,” she said. The CEO also highlighted the benefits of MultiChoice Nigeria’s integration into the Canal+ Group, which operates in more than 70 countries across Africa, Asia and Europe. She said the integration had strengthened the company’s capacity in content acquisition, technology and partnerships while retaining its focus on the Nigerian market. “We’re basically riding on global muscle, but we still want to be very relevant to the Nigerian consumer,” she stated. On the company’s transition towards digital entertainment, Omotosho said MultiChoice regarded satellite television and streaming services as complementary platforms rather than competing products. “For us, streaming is not an ‘either/or,’ it is ‘and’,” she said. She cited DStv Stream, which enables subscribers to access television content online without a satellite dish or decoder. According to her, the company’s technology-agnostic approach allows customers to choose satellite television for reliability in areas with limited broadband access or streaming services for greater flexibility. nigeria.title: AI-generated fake content threatens democracy, national security – Okonkwo
nigeria.description: By Dickson Omobola Executive Chairman of United Nigeria Airlines, Professor Obiora Okonkwo, has expressed concerns over the growing sophistication of artificial intelligence, AI, saying its capacity to generate convincing fake images, videos and voices poses fresh threats to democracy, national security and public trust, particularly during elections. Okonkwo warned that hate speech, misinformation and irresponsible communication could be as destructive as weapons, saying the 1994 Rwandan genocide was an example of how manipulated information could incite mass violence, destroy lives and destabilise nations. He spoke while delivering the opening address at the African session of the World Public Relations Forum, WPRF, Abuja 2026, where he challenged journalists, public relations practitioners, advertisers and corporate communication professionals to strengthen self-regulation and uphold ethical standards to prevent communication platforms from becoming instruments of propaganda and social division. Speaking on the theme, ‘Responsible Communication in Africa: The Importance of Self-Regulation and Information and Media Literacy,’ he said the influence of communication demanded greater responsibility from those who shaped public opinion. He said: “The lesson is unmistakable. Communication is not always an innocent exercise. In the hands of irresponsible actors, the microphone can become as disruptive as a very dangerous weapon.” He said the 2023 general elections were an example of the dangers of irresponsible communication, adding that although social media facilitated political mobilisation, it also enabled the circulation of fabricated election results, unverified claims and divisive ethnic and political narratives. He recalled that the European Union Election Observation Mission documented misleading political communication during the polls, warning that such practices could undermine public confidence in democratic institutions and citizens’ ability to make informed electoral choices. He said: “In an age of unprecedented information flow, the credibility, integrity and social value of what we communicate are as important as the freedom and the platforms through which we communicate.” The airline chairman also cited the COVID-19 pandemic, when the World Health Organisation identified an infodemic of false and misleading information that confused populations, encouraged risky behaviour and weakened confidence in public health institutions. nigeria.title: ASUU Suspends Taraba Varsity Strike After Gov Kefas’ Intervention
nigeria.description: The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Taraba State University chapter, has conditionally suspended its ongoing strike. The union resolved to suspend the total, comprehensive and indefinite strike, which began on 12 October 2026, with effect from 20 November 2026, following Governor Agbu Kefas’ approval of the full implementation of the 2025 agreement between the Federal Government and ASUU. The decision was reached at a congress held on Friday to determine the union’s position on the governor’s appeal for the suspension of the industrial action and his approval of the agreement’s implementation. This was contained in a statement issued by the ASUU chairman at Taraba State University, Garba Mbave. ASUU-TSU had embarked on the strike over the Taraba State Government’s failure to implement the 2025 Federal Government-ASUU remuneration agreement and pay outstanding salary arrears accrued from January 2026. The union had earlier engaged the state government on the demands, but commenced the indefinite industrial action on October 12 after efforts to resolve the dispute failed. A file photo of Governor of Taraba State Agbu Kefas. Photo: Facebook/Agbu Kefas The union expressed profound appreciation to Kefas, the Commissioner for Tertiary Education, the Head of Service and the university management for their interventions, constructive engagement and commitment towards resolving the industrial dispute. nigeria.title: United Nigeria Airlines begins Jos flights to Lagos, Kano, Owerri
nigeria.description: United Nigeria Airlines will commence scheduled flight operations from Jos to Lagos, Kano and Owerri on November 24 and 29, 2026, providing residents of Plateau State with additional air connections to other parts of the country. The airline said tickets for the new routes were already available for purchase. The Lagos–Jos–Lagos route will operate four times weekly on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays, while the Jos–Kano–Jos and Jos–Owerri–Jos routes will each operate twice weekly. Flights between Jos and Kano will operate on Tuesdays and Fridays, while those between Jos and Owerri will run on Wednesdays and Sundays. However, because the Owerri airport is currently closed, operations on the Jos–Owerri route will commence on Sunday, November 29, five days after the initial launch date. The development follows the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Plateau State Government and United Nigeria Airlines on Monday, November 9, at the office of the Commissioner for Transport, Jatau Gyang, in Jos. Under the agreement, the airline will introduce scheduled services on the Jos–Kano and Jos–Owerri routes, which the state government said were previously not served. Speaking after the signing, Gyang said the partnership was part of the state government’s broader efforts to position Plateau as a leading destination for investment, tourism, commerce and economic opportunities. He commended the airline’s management for its confidence in the state’s vision. According to him, the Jos–Owerri route will ease movement between Plateau and the South-East and South-South regions, thereby supporting trade, investment, tourism and social exchanges. He said the Jos–Kano connection would further strengthen Plateau’s relationship with the North-West, which he described as home to major commercial and industrial centres offering opportunities for business partnerships and trade. Responding on behalf of the airline, its Managing Director, Mazi Osita Okonkwo, said the agreement was significant because it would connect the South-East, South-West and North-Central regions. He described Plateau as a strategic state and assured that the airline would maintain its service standards. Okonkwo also commended Governor Caleb Mutfwang for his vision and strategic direction, while acknowledging Gyang’s efforts in facilitating the agreement. Passengers can book flights through the airline’s website, mobile application or accredited travel agents. nigeria.title: Fountain of Life denies closure amid leadership crisis
nigeria.description: By OLAYINKA LATONA LAGOS — The Fountain of Life Church has denied reports that its premises have been sealed, insisting that the church remains open, although access to its facilities is currently restricted amid an ongoing leadership dispute. The church, in a post on its official Instagram page, shared a graphic bearing the inscription, “DON’T BELIEVE THE NOISE! CHURCH IS NOT SEALED,” while inviting worshippers to attend its Sunday service. The clarification comes amid a leadership crisis involving Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and the church’s board, which has generated public attention in recent days. However, a visit by Vanguard correspondents to the church premises revealed restricted access, with activities appearing limited. There was no visible presence of police personnel at the premises, while private security operatives were stationed at the entrance. Efforts by a Vanguard reporter to gain access to the church were unsuccessful, as a security official said only persons with official business within the premises would be allowed in. The restricted access comes despite the church’s public invitation to worshippers to attend Sunday’s service. The church had earlier announced the postponement of its 2026 Thanksgiving Service, initially scheduled for Sunday, November 22, stating that a new date would be communicated. The developments come against the backdrop of a legal battle over the church’s leadership. The Lagos State High Court had restrained Odukoya from holding himself out as Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head of the church following an application by the church’s Incorporated Trustees. Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin granted the interim orders on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, in a suit filed by the trustees. The court also restrained Odukoya, whether acting personally or through proxies, from interfering with, disrupting or obstructing the church’s activities, governance and other operations. The orders were granted ex parte, meaning they were made without first hearing Odukoya’s response to the application. However, the court preserved his right to apply to set aside the orders or respond to the substantive claims after being served with the court processes. The case was adjourned until December 1, 2026, for mention. The leadership dispute became public on November 17, when a faction of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that it no longer recognised Odukoya as senior pastor, citing a succession video reportedly recorded by the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, in December 2021. The trustees subsequently named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader. However, Odukoya and the church leadership rejected the decision, maintaining that his appointment as senior pastor in September 2023 was valid. nigeria.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta ABEOKUTA — Former Super Eagles captain and football administrator, Chief Segun Odegbami, has sustained injuries following an attack by three armed men at his residence in Abeokuta, Ogun State. The incident reportedly occurred at about 2:30 a.m. on Friday at his residence in the Ibara Government Reservation Area (GRA). Sources in the neighbourhood said the attackers allegedly overpowered members of his domestic staff and driver before gaining access to his bedroom, where he was attacked with machetes. Odegbami, 74, is the proprietor of Eagles 7 Sports Radio 103.7 FM and a former captain of Nigeria’s national football team. A resident, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the attackers initially asked to see the former international but were told by his domestic staff that he was not at home. The source said the attackers reportedly became suspicious after noticing that the generator was running, suggesting that someone was inside the residence. According to the resident, the assailants allegedly assaulted the domestic staff before making their way into Odegbami’s bedroom, where they attacked him. The source added that Odegbami reportedly resisted the attackers during the incident, forcing them to flee the residence. He was subsequently taken to an undisclosed hospital for medical attention. The incident was reported to the police, although the motive behind the attack had yet to be established. Meanwhile, the Ogun State Commissioner of Police, Bode Ojajuni, has visited Odegbami to sympathise with him and assure him of the command’s commitment to investigating the incident. In a statement issued by the command’s spokesperson, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, the commissioner said he had ordered an immediate and thorough investigation to identify and apprehend those responsible. Ojajuni also wished the former football international a speedy recovery and assured him that the police were treating the incident seriously. The police confirmed that Odegbami had been discharged from the hospital, adding that investigative efforts were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the attack and bring those responsible to justice. The commissioner urged members of the public to remain calm and provide credible information that could assist the investigation through established police communication channels. nigeria.description: .Set to produce 6 million passports yearly By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Federal Government has begun work on a centre in Abuja that will let Nigeria manufacture its own electronic passport (e-passport) booklets for the first time, with capacity to produce six million passports a year. Minister of Interior, Hon. Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, disclosed this on Friday during the ground-breaking for the National Passport Booklet Manufacturing Centre, at the headquarters of the Nigeria Immigration Service in Abuja. “The requirement of Nigeria is roughly between 1.8 to 2 million passports a year, but by May, we will have the capacity for 6 million passports a year in production, which we are going to scale to 10 million booklets a year,” he said. The Chairman of the Senate Committee on Interior, Senator Adams Oshiomhole, broke the ground. Tunji-Ojo said the plant, which will sit on 1.1 hectares, would run off the grid and be driven by artificial intelligence. “By the time we deliver it in May, Nigeria will be the first country in West Africa to do it,” he said. He added that “there are only three countries in Africa that manufacture passports in-country”, naming South Africa, Ethiopia and Algeria. Of the three, he said, only Ethiopia has the capacity to make e-passports. The minister said the facility was not being built only for Nigeria’s needs. “What we and our partners, Iris Smart, are doing is to build a passport facility that will be able to service ECOWAS and even be able to export to other countries,” he said, referring to the Economic Community of West African States. On funding, Tunji-Ojo said the government was not footing the bill. “This project is about $70 million without a dime from government,” he said, describing Iris Smart, the vendor, as “a 100 per cent Nigerian company”. The minister disclosed that the company was first awarded an e-passport contract in 2003 under President Olusegun Obasanjo, but had been importing the booklets. He said he insisted that this must change when he assumed office. “We said we cannot be aiding employment in other countries and be creating unemployment in our own country,” he said. Tunji-Ojo said there was a heated exchange with the company over the issue. “I think the first day, I walked them out of the office. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Crashes to $59,000 as Market Selloff Deepens The bitcoin price crashed below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since early July, falling about $1,800 in roughly an hour as a deepening U.S. tech stock selloff dragged risk assets lower. Bitcoin traded near $61,400 at 9:40 a.m. ET and slid to about $59,600 by 10:45 a.m., a drop of nearly 3%, according to Look Into Bitcoin data . The bitcoin price is down about $3,400, or more than 5%, from the same time Thursday, when it traded near $63,000. The break of $60,000 is a key psychological level, and it came with little warning. Bitcoin price had held above $61,000 for most of the morning, even after a third straight daily loss. Stocks and rate hike bets drive the selloff Wall Street opened sharply lower. The Nasdaq Composite fell more than 2% in morning trading as shares of Anthropic extended losses in its second day since a record Nasdaq debut. Nvidia and AMD also traded lower. Bitcoin has been moving with tech stocks. The market has questioned whether heavy spending on artificial intelligence will pay off, and Friday’s open did nothing to ease that worry. Rate expectations are adding pressure. Traders see a roughly 94% chance the Federal Reserve raises rates in December, CME Group’s FedWatch tool showed . Higher rates tend to hurt bitcoin and other assets that pay no yield. Earlier Friday, South Korea’s Kospi index fell more than 5% and chipmakers sank across Asia. That selling carried into U.S. trading and then into bitcoin. Some analysts had flagged $60,000 as a floor. Katie Stockton of Fairlead Strategies told CNBC the bottom of bitcoin’s trading range sits “just below 60,000,” and that it “appears to be trying to find a footing.” Friday’s drop tests that view. entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. The experience opened with an exclusive session for healthcare professionals and invited guests before welcoming members of the public over the following two days. The sessions brought together healthcare professionals and representatives from across Nigeria’s dermatological beauty and skincare community, encouraging knowledge-sharing and stronger connections between science, expertise and consumer education. Visitors explored five dedicated Innovation Corners showcasing La Roche-Posay’s Effaclar, Mela B3, Anthelios, Cicaplast and Lipikar ranges. Each space introduced visitors to specific skin concerns and the science behind the brand’s product formulations. Through interactive demonstrations and guided product experiences, guests gained a better understanding of different skin concerns and the role of targeted skincare in addressing them. At the Anthelios corner, visitors used a UV camera to see the effects of ultraviolet exposure and better understand the importance of sun protection. We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time. It’s just a different game playing in the Big Ten than in the Big XII when it comes to not only the talent on the field, but the expectations, media coverage, etc. He was super conservative in some early season games and it bit the Lions in home losses to Wisconsin and USC. Most on our staff looked at the schedule and thought this team should go at least 8-4/9-3. They still might get to 8-4, but there has certainly been some frustration. The schedule was light – Penn State didn’t play Oregon or Ohio State or Indiana. I think there was some hope that this team could follow the same template Curt Cignetti did at IU (bring over a bunch of guys familiar with the program, take advantage of an easy schedule, slide into the playoff and build some momentum). sports.title: Filming training by drones should be illegal - Iraola
sports.description: Andoni Iraola's Liverpool take on Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United on Sunday [Getty Images] Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola says filming with drones around training grounds should be illegal after Mauricio Pochettino's first session as Manchester United boss was captured and uploaded online. Pochettino and his players were clearly visible in the footage, which was shot above United's Carrington training base from a variety of angles and distances. The drone operater apologised and later took down the footage, with sources telling BBC Sport they are adamant there was no security breach and that they do not intend to take legal action. Iraola said he was sent the 12 minutes of footage on Thursday - three days before United travel to Anfield for a Premier League match. "The important part of this is that it shouldn't be legal," he said on Friday. "It happened to United but it could happen to me. "Yesterday, when Sky Sports had access to our training and the cameras recorded 15-20 minutes, you know who trained and who didn't. "It's not the matter of the advantage. It's the fact that someone can do this. There's a reason we train behind closed doors because there are some things that you have to respect. I don't think it's nice for any club." Ten outfield players were seen working directly with former United States boss Pochettino in the footage, though it seems unlikely they will all start Sunday's match. "We've faced each other and obviously he [Pochettino] has a lot of Premier League games behind him that we can look at," said Iraola. "We can look at games from the US but it's true that they have this small advantage that we don't have references to prepare, because they can go different ways that we honestly don't know right now." Iraola said he expected United to be "well prepared" as Pochettino's assistants travelled to England to work with the players before the Argentine arrived on Wednesday. "They have this advantage that we don't exactly know - or at least we don't have the references like we do against other opposition," he said. "Especially the beginning of the game will be important. We have to adapt to certain things. But we know the players very well." Liverpool are fourth in the table - 14 places ahead of United. But they have failed to beat the Red Devils at Anfield in each of the past three seasons, and have lost to Arsenal and Manchester City at home already in this campaign. "You don't find bigger games than this," said Iraola. "I feel lucky to be here and privileged to be a part of these games. "We have to acknowledge the importance of the game. There are a lot of ingredients. They have a new manager, new challenges for us. This is important for us in a lot of different ways. "We want to improve our form at home. We have been very good away but not good at home and the first chance we have is United on Sunday." Pochettino training session filmed by drone - what did we learn? sports.description: Enzo Maresca's Manchester City have lost their past three Premier League matches (Darren Staples) Enzo Maresca insists his Manchester City players are not distracted by the "noise" around the club's financial-rules case as he seeks to end their losing run. City flew out of the blocks in the Premier League this season, winning their first seven games, but three straight defeats have left them six points behind leaders Arsenal. The 10-time English champions are still waiting to discover the extent of their punishment after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules. The club have repeatedly denied wrongdoing and have appealed against the verdict. But Maresca said he did not believe the case was weighing on the minds of his third-placed team ahead of their match against Fulham at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday. "I don't think the players are thinking too much about that," he said, "If we want to relate the noise with the defeats, Villa away, I think we had so many chances... Brighton here, the keeper was the man of the match. "The Forest one (a 3-1 defeat), where Erling (Haaland) had the chance to (make it) 2-2. I don't think the players are focused on the noise." Maresca admitted his side needed to improve but said not everything was perfect even when they were winning. "Overall, we control the game almost every time," said the Italian. "There are moments when we don't control the game and it is a moment when we need to understand the reason why and to do better." The former Chelsea boss, who replaced Pep Guardiola in the close-season, pointed out that he had not been at City for long, stressing his focus is on the long term. "Probably you forget a little bit about the time we spent together," he said. "It is not a big time that we are together. That is why I can see that what we are working on every day is there. "This is a good thing, it is a nice feeling. Also, the work we are doing is helping the players to be better players and to be a better team. For me, it is just the beginning of something long." sports.title: The tale of the Wolves fans who did not return from a world cup to be shown
sports.description: The documentary follows the adventures of a group of Wolves fans who went to the Mexico World Cup in 1986 and never came back to the UK [Gary Allen] A screening of a documentary about a group of Wolves fans who went to the 1986 World Cup in Mexico and did not return to the Black Country will take place at the club. The group decided not to return to their Stourbridge and Lye homes after attending the global football spectacular, embarking on new lives in the US instead. Gary Allen, who settled in Atlanta and who pitched the documentary, said "Wolves called us and said 'would you like to do the first screening in the UK at the Molineux? And of course all being Wolves fans we said 'we'd love to'." Lost Down Mexico Way will be shown at Molineux on Friday evening, just one part of reunion gatherings this week. The stars of the documentary are referred to by their nicknames. As well as Allen, known as Adder, it features Rabbithead (Garry Hardwicke), Batesy (Stuart Bates), Arnie (David Arnold) and Texas Steve (Steve Dawson). After the World Cup and a brief jaunt to Belize, the gang flew to Dallas, Texas. Gary Allen, known as Adder, said "before you know it, there's 40 years gone" [Gary Allen] The group had lived in the Black Country all their lives before flying 5,000 miles to experience the 1986 tournament. Allen, who retired from running his own company last year, has previously said the "opportunity was the biggest thing for us", as he talked about the US. "I think back in 86... the job situation wasn't the best back then. "I'd just lost my job, [Margaret] Thatcher was in power, a few of the lads were just doing painting and whatever. "We'd all saved a bit of money and the idea was to go out there and do a few weeks and just travel. We just played it by ear really." Allen added once "we got there and enjoyed it, it just went from there and we all stayed and then more and more came over". "And before you know it, there's 40 years gone," he said. "So it was just a chance we took back in the day and luckily it's panned out well for us." Of those attending, a coach from Stourbridge was leaving on Friday afternoon "and about four or five carloads". "So we've got 80 [in] total that Wolves have given us tickets for, so it should be a good reunion," Allen added. Allen said he was looking forward to having a "good chat, good reminisce". "As you get older you can't do it. "So this is a one-off and it'll be the last time I see a lot of people, but it's gonna be great and we'll certainly make the most of it." sports.description: FILE PHOTO - USA manager and new Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino during press conference at the Arthur M. Blank National Training Centre. Pochettino has been appointed as Manchester United head coach from November 18, the club have announced. (is associated with: «Pochettino outlines his expectations in first Man Utd press conference») Press Association/PA Wire/dpa Mauricio Pochettino wants a say in “all the main decisions” around Manchester United’s squad after arriving as the club’s new head coach this week. Pochettino addressed the media for the first time as United boss on Friday, two days before the trip to face old rivals Liverpool – a match United will start inside the relegation zone. United’s recent recruitment has come in for heavy criticism with a feeling that Pochettino’s predecessor Michael Carrick was left short-handed by the club’s summer business, overseen by director of football Jason Wilcox. While he has accepted the title of head coach, former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino made clear he wants to have a big say behind the scenes. “Since I started at Espanyol, head coach, coach, manager…in the end it’s not changing too much, because I think the way that we work is indifferent to the title description,” Pochettino said. “Sometimes I worked much better when I was head coach or when I was coach than manager, and it’s not necessarily that if you are manager you have all the decisions. Maybe you are a coach and have more power in the decision. “It depends on the structure, depends on the communication, depends on the relationship with all the areas. I know that being a head coach I am the guy that is going to decide the squad for Sunday, I’m going to pick the starting 11 and make the changes. “Of course in the future I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that will happen on the squad. However, even after winning their seventh division title in ten years, they ran into the Dodgers who managed to shutdown their bats and knock them out of the postseason in the NLDS 3-1. We talked to Ivan the Great of Battery Power about their takeaways from the 2026 season and what the Braves can look forward to in 2027. With the 2026 season in the rearview mirror, what do team fans think are the key takeaways, both good and bad on the season? I think this is one of those things where asking five Braves fans will give you seven opinions. On top of that, the Braves had a very strange 2026 season, which only makes the narrative more complicated. The good is that the Braves ended up where they were expected to be: lots of wins, on top of the division. The bad is that 2026 was Year Two of “some component of the organization has no idea what to do offensively.” After a very specific offensive approach that we jokingly call “The PowerPoint” from 2019-2024, the Braves pivoted away from it hard in 2025 to disastrous results – and 2026 was a mixed bag of stuff that sometimes looked like 2019-2024, sometimes looked like 2025, and often just felt like flailing for a life preserver. The young wing-back sustained the serious injury just six minutes after coming on against Charlton Athletic and has since undergone surgery. “He’s had an operation. He’s going to be out for 12 months,” Wilder said. “You know, straight away. I think we all knew where that was going. How he awkwardly landed, and straight away, I think you always go on the reaction of the players. “It’s a testing time for him and a testing time for us because we’re losing a really attack-minded player that we were looking forward to getting back amongst us. “He was finding his feet. He was coming off the bench, and he probably would have been in contention to start now, but that’s not the case. I’m gonna have to get on with it.” Wilder also provided an update on Ryan One, who is likely to remain unavailable until the start of 2027 after suffering a setback in training. “He’s about a month or six weeks away,” Wilder said. “So, I think the start of 2027, he’ll be back. We’re going to have to take a little bit more time with him.”

Initially, he thought the teammate was joking. But after speaking directly with Goff, he realized the situation was legitimate. “So I’m sitting there. I’m like, ‘This is my first touchdown of the season, and I’m in Germany. technology.title: AI boom threatens circuit board crunch to rival pandemic-era chip shortage
technology.description: The electronics industry faces a printed circuit board (PCB) shortage that could rival the pandemic-era chip crunch – with AI once again accused of hogging supplies. The Global Electronics Association says demand is arriving "at a scale the supply chain was not built for," straining everything from glass fabric and resin to finished boards. Its report, " The PCB Squeeze: A Wake-Up Call for Global Electronics ," says AI servers need increasingly complex boards. While a typical PC board has about 12 layers of tracks, AI server boards can have 40 to 60 layers or more, and each additional layer requires more resin, copper foil, and laminate. The supply of materials is set to be constrained through at least the first half of 2027, the report says, with meaningful relief unlikely before mid-2028. Programs to deliver PCBs for automotive, industrial, medical and even the defense industries are being crowded out as AI soaks up scarce capacity, it claims. The association's North American figures show orders growing much faster than deliveries. PCB bookings rose 56.1 percent in the first nine months of 2026 compared with the same period last year, while PCB shipments increased 13.3 percent. Fabrication capacity is expanding, aimed at meeting the increased demand from the AI infrastructure sector, especially in Asia, where more than 90 percent of the world's boards are made. The report says that $10 billion has gone toward new PCB plants in Southeast Asia, and at least as much has been invested in China over the past three years, but the raw materials are themselves constrained. It warns of lengthening lead times for those raw materials. Standard FR-4 laminate now takes six to eight weeks to ship, up from two to three weeks a year ago, while advanced low-loss laminates now take 14 to 18 weeks for delivery, for example. Tightening supplies usually lead to price increases, and the report says that suppliers raised laminate costs by 30 percent in September, and that the price tag of some types of E-glass cloth for circuit boards has risen by 300 percent. The report also puts copper prices up 37 percent over the past year. Concerns have been raised about copper supplies before, as The Register has reported multiple times. The association compares the risk with the 2021 chip shortage , when disrupted supplies left manufacturers unable to secure even relatively mundane components. New capacity is coming, but it is late and comes in dribs and drabs, according to the report, while AI demand just keeps on absorbing it as soon as it arrives. The association's advice is for buyers to plan early, and to share realistic forecasts with suppliers rather than double-booking. Board makers should qualify alternative suppliers of materials such as laminate and copper foil before shortages bite, but it warns against stockpiling beyond real need, which adds to forward-buying pressure. technology.title: 'Critical' 1970s-era Fujitsu UK police system could remain unsupported for three years
technology.description: The UK's Home Office faces running the Police National Computer (PNC) without vendor support for three years or more as it misses another deadline to decommission the ageing crime-fighting system first introduced in 1974. The PNC was first launched in 1974, when Tom Baker began his iconic role playing Doctor Who, and has seen the tenure of 26 UK Home Secretaries, surviving multiple efforts to replace it. A notice in December 2024 said that the Home Office was "focused on the development and adoption of the Law Enforcement Data Service (LEDS) products to replace existing PNC capability across all police forces and other non-policing PNC consumers, enabling the retirement by March 2026 (the point at which PNC support will expire)." We understand that PNC support refers to the Fujitsu support contract for the mainframe, which is housed in north London. Support for the Software AG database on the mainframe OS (BS2000) ran out at the end of 2024. So the database holding the crucial police data remains out of standard support and potentially will stay that way until 2027. The decommissioning date for the PNC had already been pushed back by the need to delay and "reset" the LEDS in 2020. The Home Office launched its successor, National Law Enforcement Data Service, in 2016, and planned to finish the new system by 2020 at a cost of £671 million. The Home Office told The Register this week that it needed more time, and it aimed to begin decommissioning the system from March 2027, raising questions over how it would be supported. A Home Office spokesperson said: "We are modernizing policing systems to adapt to evolving challenges, including rolling out the LEDS to replace the Police National Computer. "While LEDS is already operational, we are continuing to run the legacy Police National Computer system to support the operational needs of all UK police," they said. Officials said the PNC would remain available throughout the transition and would only be disconnected when police forces have confirmed that they no longer need it. Earlier this month, in a written response in the House of Lords, Lord Hanson of Flint, a junior minister, said the PNC might be required until early 2028. Some LEDS services were already live and the program was "targeting completion of the remaining development, adoption and readiness activity in early 2027 as we prepare for our final stages for LEDS deployment before retiring the PNC," he said. "Once the transition of all police users to the LEDS has been completed and policing has confirmed that the PNC is no longer required, the system will be disconnected and decommissioned. The decommissioning process is expected to take place between late 2027 and early 2028," he said . technology.title: US will soon announce root cause behind FAA nationwide ground stop
technology.description: The US government will announce soon the root cause of the router outage that led to the third-ever nationwide ground stop issued by the US Federal Aviation Administration. But questions remain about whether the FAA's effort to modernize the national airspace system is being done with all the proper risk assessments and adequate agency oversight of the private contractors involved. The nationwide ground stop forced about 3,500 aircraft to immediately land and impacted more than 1 million passengers across the United States in the middle of the afternoon on Friday, November 13. More than 12,000 flights were canceled on that day alone, with the number rising to more than 20,000 over the weekend as stranded travelers scrambled to find accommodations or alternative transportation. Nearly one week later, FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford told news reporters that government investigators are “very close” to figuring out the root cause of the nationwide ground stop, according to CNN . technology.title: Microsoft's last non-security preview of 2026 packs a punch
technology.description: Microsoft has delivered its final scheduled non-security preview update of 2026 for Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2, with an updated Windows Search experience and a brighter Windows Hello for users who prefer darker rooms. The optional KB5132057 update arrived on November 19, after this month's Patch Tuesday. Microsoft is skipping December's non-security preview because of reduced holiday operations, though that doesn't cancel the monthly security release. This last preview is quite a doozy. The big-ticket item is the "new Windows Search Experience." We saw a preview of this last month, and Microsoft has gone well beyond the "just make it work" request of many Windows users. Results appear faster with less clutter, the tool uses memory better, and files can be previewed directly in Windows Search. We're less convinced by inline actions, which let users perform common tasks directly through Windows Search without opening Settings. In our testing, "turn on dark mode" worked, but "switch on dark mode" did not, thus highlighting the limitations of the tool. In addition, we remain unconvinced that Windows Search is the place to run actions. That said, anything that makes Windows Search less of a punchline for unkind jokes about performance and accuracy is welcome, as are other features, including an optional screen-brightening feature for Windows Hello facial recognition in dim rooms, and the PowerToys-esque Run dialog, which users can enable in Settings. While some of the new features won't be enabled immediately, Microsoft has included fixes that will be available right away. One addresses an issue where Windows Fax and Scan could fail to connect to a fax server. Handy for those occasions when email falls over into a heap . There are also fixes for Windows IoT Enterprise LTSC activation failures and the misleading "Something went wrong" message shown on Android devices during cross-device passkey authentication. At the time of writing, Microsoft still lists the problem as something for which "we are working on a resolution to be released in a future Windows update." Sadly, not everything has been pushed off the naughty step. SQL Server queries using OLE DB providers can still leave connections to external databases open after they've finished. Microsoft is working on that one and "will provide an update in an upcoming release." ®

technology.title: Microsoft suggests Registry hack to work around hotpatch woes
technology.description: Some Windows 11 applications might fail to install or launch after Microsoft's November hotpatch, but not to worry: there's a Registry tweak to work around it. Microsoft has confirmed it isn't administrators' imaginations. The November hotpatch is causing application errors, including in little-used and obscure apps such as Outlook. Affected applications may fail during installation, launch, or use, displaying errors such as " ERROR_ALLOTTED_SPACE_EXCEEDED (0xC0000099) ." Microsoft's investigation points to applications that load the 32-bit Windows Installer DLL, msi.dll. The problem is more common with 32-bit software, but can also affect 64-bit applications "under certain circumstances." The workaround involves fiddling with the Registry on affected devices, so is not for the faint of heart and a backup is a good idea before diving in. Microsoft says the key " HotPatchTableSize " in the folder " HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management " needs to be set to " 2000 " followed by a restart. Just the thing to round out the week for administrators. The issue affects the November hotpatch, not the standard monthly cumulative security update. "Devices which installed the November 2026 Windows monthly security update are not expected to be affected by this issue," Microsoft said. Windows hotpatches are security updates that don't require a device restart (unless, as in this instance, administrators have to do so to address errors after a hotpatch is installed). Windows 11 hotpatching requires version 24H2 or later, an eligible subscription, and the necessary management and security configuration. "Hotpatch update package size is significantly smaller than the standard cumulative updates," Microsoft said, and the goal is to "streamline the installation process and enhance compliance efficiency." The offending hotpatch, KB5132043 , was released on November 10. It followed the October 13 baseline , which was a prerequisite. Microsoft made hotpatching the default in Windows Autopatch earlier this year. At the time, we asked: " What could possibly go wrong? " Thanks to November's hotpatch, we have our answer. ®
